item.title: Marine spatial planning in southern Brazil
item.description:
How to allocate the ocean space among competing users?

PEM Sul is the national pilot for marine spatial planning in Brazil, covering the southern marine region across Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul. The work develops spatially explicit indicators (including a composite Performance Index) to support sustainable, multi-sector ocean management.

Context

Marine spatial planning (MSP) is a public, participatory process for distributing human activities across marine space, targeting ecological, economic, and social objectives simultaneously. In Brazil, the ocean accounts for roughly 19% of GDP across some 5.7 million km² of national jurisdiction. Managing that space without accumulating conflicts requires more than sectoral regulation; it requires a spatial framework.
